messages:
sam: FYI I hit a repeatable p95 spike in a tenant that mixes tiny KV lookups and occasional long generations after enabling aggressive prefetching. Baseline ~20ms, spike ~55ms.

lee: Was prefetching pulling more host pages into staging and hitting eviction pressure?

sam: Traces show: kvcache.lookup -> prefetch_coalesce -> host-stage pin -> dma_submit -> queue_wait. Many prefetch ops pushed dma queue into saturation for ~40ms windows.

anya: So two problems: prefetch volume + queue saturation, and allocator fragmentation in host pool causing pin stalls. Any tenant tokens in place?

sam: We have a naive per-tenant concurrency cap but it's loose. The tenant overloaded tiny allocations and prefetches concurrently.

lee: Proposal: adaptive admission controller that issues "prefetch tokens" and "tiny-slot tokens" independently. Prefetch tokens throttle the number of outstanding staged pages a tenant can request; tiny-slot tokens limit cheap fastpath allocations from tiny arenas. Tokens refill based on observed dma_queue_util and slab_free_percent.

anya: Interesting. How does refill work? PID? heuristics?

lee: Start simple: two thresholds for dma_queue_util: low(<30%), mid(30-70%), high(>70%). When low, ramp tokens up; when high, decay tokens exponentially. Combine with slab_free_percent: if slabs are >70% used, reduce tiny-slot tokens to avoid wasting slabs.

sam: Sounds practical. Also consider prioritizing prefetches: emergency pin for active generation vs background prefetch. Active RPCs get reserved tokens; background prefetches are best-effort and receive lower priority.

anya: We'll need metrics: tenant_prefetch_outstanding, tenant_tiny_slots_used, dma_queue_util, slab_free_percent, and token_grant_rate. Also an event stream for token throttles to correlate with tails.

lee: Implementation sketch: admission sits in kvcache layer. On lookup miss: if request qualifies as prefetch (heuristic: likely-needed pages ahead), check tenant_prefetch_tokens, if zero queue the prefetch async or drop it. For tiny allocs, fastpath checks tiny-slot tokens; if zero, fallback to slow allocator.

sam: Fallback to slow allocator will increase latency for that RPC, but prevents global DMA saturation. Need to ensure fairness; maybe a cheap retry window for prefetch tokens with backoff.

anya: We should also add a global burst bucket for brief spikes: tenants can borrow extra tokens for short windows if host_cpu_idle and dma_queue_util allow. Borrowing tracked and repaid by longer refill cooldown.

lee: Edgecases: cross-tenant compaction races; if compaction frees slabs while a tenant borrows tokens, token accounting must be conservative. Also token state must survive scheduler failovers. Store token state in local cache with periodic drain/resync to control plane.

sam: Can token checks be lockless and cheap? This is on hot path. Atomic decrement with CAS should be fine. If we need to queue, move to async worker.

anya: Testing plan: add a harness with mixed workloads: 80% tiny-KV (20-512B), 20% long-gen. Inject prefetch aggressiveness param and run across dma_queue_util ranges. Capture p50/p95/p99 and host mem footprint.

lee: Rollout: feature-flagged admission in staging for noisy tenants. Start with conservative defaults: prefetch_tokens=32, tiny_tokens=128, global_burst=64. Observe dma_queue_util and adjust thresholds.

devops-bot: Opened EXP-2024-55: "prefetch + tiny-slot admission controller experiment" assigned [sam, lee, anya].

sam: Next: I'll prototype token checkout in kvcache and add metrics. Lee please draft the refill policy doc; Anya build the mixed workload harness.

anya: Will add telemetry dashboards and a tracing span on token operations. Also a debug flag to force token exhaustion for repro.

lee: We should also consider a soft prefetch cancellation: if dma_queue_util rises while a prefetch is in-flight, we should be able to cancel aggregated prefetches that are not yet needed. That reduces wasted DMA cycles.

sam: Good call. Combine with per-microbatch coalesce: only issue prefetch for microbatches above a threshold or when tokens are ample.

anya: Ok. Aim for an initial staging experiment next week. If we see p95 improvements without too much host mem increase, we can expand rollout. :+1:
